description: SIM-05 validation cases of Heuretes FreeCAD: published reference values with citations (numbers only), and the parameters of the geometry builders in bruceworx_validation_cases.py. Run by bruceworx_validation.py.

cfd.title: Actuator disk in hover, Rankine-Froude momentum theory

references.label: mean axial velocity through the disk (induced velocity v_i)
references.basis: v_i = sqrt(T / (2 rho A)) with T = 1 N, D = 76 mm, rho = 1.204 kg/m^3 (20 C, sea level): 9.567 m/s. Uniform actuator disk, steady RANS k-omega SST; the RANS result sits 7 to 8 % high and tends to 9.6 to 10.2 m/s on finer meshes.

references.label: mean axial velocity in the contracted wake core (r < 0.6 R, 0.9 to 1.1 D downstream)
references.basis: Far wake 2 v_i = 19.13 m/s in momentum theory (ideal, no mixing); the turbulent shear layer mixes the wake, so the core sits 10 to 13 % low at 1 D (the check allows 15 %).

citation.document: Rankine-Froude momentum theory of an actuator disk in hover (any rotor text; e.g. J. G. Leishman, Principles of Helicopter Aerodynamics, 2nd ed., chapter 2)
citation.location: ideal induced velocity v_i = sqrt(T/(2 rho A)); the fully developed wake velocity is 2 v_i

cfd.licence: closed-form result of a textbook theory; no tabulated data is copied
cfd.setup: Axisymmetric 5 degree wedge about the X axis, 4 D upstream, 14 D downstream, 5 D radius, all outer faces open (totalPressure); one disk of 76 mm diameter and D/8 thickness at x = 0 with a constant momentum force of 1 N on the air (+X), simpleFoam k-omega SST, bruceworx_cfd_wash.write_disk_case.

cases.title: NAFEMS LE10, thick elliptic plate under pressure

references.label: sigma_yy at D (2, 0, 0.6) m, top surface at the hole
references.basis: NAFEMS target; NEGATIVE = compressive. Confirmed: COMSOL model documentation states the NAFEMS value as -5.38 MPa; the FeenoX/Fino example (hex20, same BCs) computes -5.38016 / -5.3601 MPa with the pressure pressing down on the top face; this build gives -5.34 MPa (mesh 120 mm) with the same sign. Altair and Abaqus quote the magnitude 5.38 only.

references.label: radial displacement at C (R, 0, L)

references.basis: the manual's beam theory at z = 2R: M(z) = q0 (L - z)^3 / (6 L), sigma = M R / I, I = pi R^4 / 4, with q0 = 3 N/mm, L = 240 mm; at z = 0 the same formula gives the manual's 169.8 MPa

references.label: sigma_zz at B (R, 0, 0), the clamped section
references.basis: the manual's value is beam theory at the root. The 3D solid has a root effect that depends on the clamp: 164 MPa with the section held plane (this case), about 220 MPa with a fully clamped face (mesh-converged, 1 mm), so it is reported but not marked.

cases.licence: GNU Free Documentation Licence (stated in the PDF): the numbers are stored with this citation, the PDF is not

Root: z=0 face held in z only (the section stays plane and may contract), rigid motions removed at the two points (+-R, 0, 0). Geometry check: R, L and the load are from section 1; the beam values 1.552e-3 m and 169.8 MPa follow from q0 L^4/(30 E I) and q0 L^2 R/(6 I).

cases.title: NAFEMS FV52, simply supported solid square plate
cases.note: The flexural modes converge 2.5 to 5 % below the NAFEMS targets (mode 4: 43.6, 43.4, 43.0 Hz on the 600, 400, 300 mm meshes against 45.897, still falling as the mesh is refined) with the support as the ANSYS manual states it (uz=0 on the bottom edges); with the support at mid-height 44.0 Hz, with the whole side faces held in z 44.3 Hz (500 mm mesh). The in-plane mode 8 (193.59 Hz) matches to 0.01 %, so E, nu and the density are right. Not made to match; reported as a known gap, tolerance unchanged.

diameter_check.result: D = 0.2 m is the DIAMETER (R = 0.1 m)

cases.setup: The whole steel annulus a=10, b=50 mm, 2 mm thick (no symmetry planes), E=210 GPa, nu=0.3, rho=7850 kg/m3, spinning at 30 000 rpm about Z. Held only by bruceworx_sim_post.hold_for_spin: point A (nearest the axis) holds both directions across the axis, point B on the +X radius holds the tangential direction Y, and the axial direction is held along the circular edge at A's level (a plain annulus has no third vertex off the A-B line). A balanced rotor has no reaction at these points, so the bore and rim hoop stress (the mean of the nodes on each circle) are the free disc's; a Fixed bore would stop the bore growing and is refused by the pre-check. The 3D thin disc differs from plane stress by a fraction of a percent.

cases.title: Spin, then vibration modes: rotating cantilever beam, flapping modes (centrifugal stiffening)

references.label: flapping mode 1, omega / sqrt(E I / rho A L^4), eta = 3 (unspun 3.5160)
flapping mode 2, omega / sqrt(E I / rho A L^4), eta = 3 (unspun 22.0345)

citation.document: Wright, Smith, Thresher and Wang, Vibration modes of centrifugally stiffened beams, J. Appl. Mech. 49 (1982) 197-202: exact (Frobenius series) out-of-plane frequencies of the uniform cantilever with zero hub radius. Values read from their reproduction as 'Exact [1]' in Table 4 of Rodrigues, Alazard, Sanfedino, Mauriello and Iannelli, Modeling and analysis of a flexible spinning Euler-Bernoulli beam with centrifugal stiffening and softening (ISAE-SUPAERO, arXiv:2401.17519): out-of-plane mode 1 = 3.5160, 4.7973, 7.3604, 13.1702 and mode 2 = 22.0345, 23.3203, 26.8091, 37.6031 at eta = 0, 3, 6, 12; eta = Omega sqrt(rho A L^4 / (E I))
citation.location: arXiv:2401.17519 Table 4 (rows 'Exact [1]', out-of-plane, eta = 3 column); the values were also reproduced to 5 digits by an independent Rayleigh-Ritz computation (TestBruceWorxValidation, 12 cantilever modes)

cases.licence: Published numerical values (facts) quoted with their source; no text or figures copied
cases.setup: Steel cantilever 500 x 20 x 10 mm (flap thickness h = 10 mm, L/h = 50, so Euler-Bernoulli applies to better than 0.5 percent for modes 1 and 2), clamped at x = 0 on the axis of rotation (zero hub radius). Study steps Stationary + Eigenfrequency (SIM-07): a static CalculiX step with a Centrifugal load of 1710.95 rpm about Z (eta = 3, i.e. Omega = 179.2 rad/s; the first flapping frequency rises 36 percent, 33.4 to 45.6 Hz), then *STEP, PERTURBATION *FREQUENCY about that state. The flapping modes (bending in z, out of the plane of rotation) are the modes with their modal mass in z; reported as f / sqrt(E I / rho A L^4). The first in-plane (lead-lag) frequency is measured as lead1 and not compared: CalculiX's perturbation step carries the centrifugal tension (stiffening) but not the rotating-frame softening term, so its in-plane modes are those of a stationary beam under the centrifugal tension. The Southwell estimate omega^2 = omega0^2 + K Omega^2 with the Rayleigh-quotient K1 = 1.1933 (about 1.19; computed in the test) gives 4.806 for mode 1 (0.2 percent above the exact value).
